messages:
lisa_custsuccess: Customer report: tenant t-87a seeing sudden p95/p99 latency regressions and ~1% 500s since 11:04 UTC. P95 ~1.6s, p99 ~6-8s. Sending logs below, can you triage?
jess_support: Thanks — opening escalation. Which model and pool is this hitting? Any OOMs in runtime?
lisa_custsuccess: Model: redwood-rt/vicuna-13b-4bit, region us-west-2, dedicated pool on A100-80GB. Logs show repeated "out of memory during allocation" and 500s. Repro curl: `curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -d '{"model":"vicuna-13b","input":"<long prompt>","max_tokens":1024}'`
jess_support: Got it. Tagging runtime + SRE. @matt_runtime @olga_sre
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3289, severity: high, owner: jess_support
matt_runtime: Looking at node stats. Initial observation: per-tenant KV cache grew ~4x in last 3 hours and slab fragmentation is up. Likely KV growth + fragmentation causing allocation failures -> fallback to slow path -> p99 spike.
olga_sre: Can you paste the runtime OOM logs and allocator stats?
lisa_custsuccess: Paste logs: ```
[2026-03-16T11:03:57Z] ERROR runtime: GPU OOM: failed to allocate 1.2GiB
[2026-03-16T11:04:01Z] WARN  kv: tenant=t-87a kv_entries=134214 kv_evicted=0
[2026-03-16T11:04:01Z] INFO  allocator: slab_total=48GiB slab_free=24MiB fragmentation=74%
[2026-03-16T11:04:02Z] ERROR api: 500 internal server error, trace=tr_0abc
```
matt_runtime: Confirming: fragmentation 74% is very high. kv_evicted=0 indicates eviction is disabled or stuck. Are they using default eviction?
jess_support: Customer says dedicated pool default had eviction disabled for safety. They didn't expect kv to grow unbounded.
matt_runtime: Temporary mitigations: reduce max_tokens to 256 or route heavy requests to CPU fallback to avoid large KV allocations; enable kv_ttl or LRU eviction for this tenant as emergency; schedule rolling restart with slab_defrag enabled.
david_oncall: I can patch pool config and restart a single node canary. Will take host-rt-23 as canary in ~5m.
matt_runtime: Longer term: allocator tuning — lower slab growth and enable background defrag. Proposal: allocator.slab_target_util=0.65 and slab_defrag=true, plus per-tenant soft limits on kv cache and prefix eviction.
jess_support: Customer requests immediate relief. Applying kv_ttl=10m for tenant t-87a now.
ops-bot: Config change applied: kv_ttl=10m for tenant t-87a by jess_support
olga_sre: Canary restart started on host-rt-23. Monitoring memory and latency.
matt_runtime: Canary results: p99 dropped to ~1.4s on canary, fragmentation down to ~42%, GPU allocations succeeding.
olga_sre: Looks promising. Recommend rolling restart of remaining nodes after 30m validation window.
lisa_custsuccess: Customer reports partial improvement — p99 back to ~1.5s but occasional spikes remain. They want notes about what changed and why.
jess_support: We'll schedule full pool restart and follow up. Matt/Olga please prepare release notes and rollback plan. Also add suggestion to customers: route long-context workloads to quantized int8 variant or set shorter max_tokens.
matt_runtime: Will open PR for allocator default changes and add runbook steps: `runtime metrics kv_entries slab_frag` and quick fixes `set-kv-ttl --tenant t-87a 10m` and `restart-node --host host-rt-XX --canary`.
olga_sre: Also adding an alert: page when slab_frag > 60% sustained for 10m to catch these earlier.
lisa_custsuccess: Please also ask customer to provide a short trace if they can reproduce (X-Trace header) so we can correlate request -> KV growth.
jess_support: Please collect a short trace token from customer if reproducible. Closing thread as in-progress; will follow up with postmortem once rolling restart and PR merged.
ops-bot: INC-2026-3289 status: in-progress -> mitigated (partial)
lisa_custsuccess: ack :thumbsup:
